method: Every note in research/notes/ was matched against the six review/hyperresearch/ deliverables plus review/outstanding-fetches.md by title, arXiv id and DOI; ~38 notes showed no match, and each was opened and triaged. research/temp/claims-*.json and research/temp/jga-venue-set.md were then read for extracted claims that no deliverable consumed.

findings.issue: The two strongest NEGATIVE results in the literature about hearing orbifold isotropy — the exact quantity Theorem C claims to recover — are absent from Q3's competitor analysis. Q3 stress-tests the priority claim against Bari-Hunsicker, Ucar, Dryden-Strohmaier, Doyle-Rossetti, Linowitz-Voight and a 12-query arXiv sweep, but never mentions Shams-Stanhope-Webb, 'One cannot hear orbifold isotropy type', or Rossetti-Schueth-Weilandt, 'Isospectral orbifolds with different maximal isotropy orders' — both of which the manuscript itself cites (\bibitem{ssw2006}, \bibitem{rsw2008}). SSW appears in the deliverables only once, as a page-range correction in VERDICT.md row 8. A referee — and Schueth, a first-tier referee on Q5's own list, is an RSW author — will open Theorem C and immediately ask how a paper titled 'One cannot hear orbifold isotropy type' coexists with 'three heat coefficients determine the cone-order multiset'. The reconciliation is already extracted in the vault and simply was not used.
findings.evidence: Note `one-cannot-hear-orbifold-isotropy-type-archiv-der-mathematik-springer-nature-lin` (Arch. Math. (Basel) 87 (2006) no. 4, 375-385, DOI 10.1007/s00013-006-1748-0), abstract verbatim: 'We show that the isotropy types of the singularities of Riemannian orbifolds are not determined by the Laplace spectrum. Indeed, we construct arbitrarily large families of mutually isospectral orbifolds with different isotropy types. Finally, we show that the corresponding singular strata of two isospectral orbifolds may not be homeomorphic.' Note `07102432-isospectral-orbifolds-with-different-maximal-isotropy-orders` (arXiv:0710.2432) and `isospectral-orbifolds-with-different-maximal-isotropy-orders-annals-of-global-an` (Ann. Global Anal. Then, after the closing sentence of section 4 ('...consistent with — and is in fact implied by — the manuscript's own Theorem C.'), add one paragraph: 'The manuscript should draw this contrast explicitly rather than leaving both papers in the bibliography undescribed. Saying so in §1.3 costs one sentence and pre-empts the obvious referee objection.'

findings.issue: The manuscript proves its two finite-trigonometric-sum identities from scratch (Lemma 2.1, sum cot^2(j pi/m) = (m-1)(m-2)/3, and Proposition 2.2, sum csc^2(j pi/m) = (m^2-1)/3) and §1.3(b) calls them 'classical', but attaches no citation. The vault holds the exact citation DGGW themselves use for the same family of sums, plus a 2024 survey of the whole family, plus Ucar's own treatment — and no deliverable mentions any of them. Q2 even quotes DGGW's sin^{-4} identity, (m^4+10m^2-11)/45, without saying where DGGW got it. This is a Q2 sub-question ('record the EXACT stated formula ... and any conventions') left unanswered, and it is the cheapest fix in the whole sweep: a 'classical' claim with no reference is exactly what a Springer copy-editing pass and a referee both flag.

See [3] and the references therein or [7, 16] for evaluations of this and similar finite trigonometric sums.' Note `1213972406` (the DGGW Crossref record) resolves [3]: 'B. C. Berndt and B. P. Yeap, Explicit evaluations and reciprocity theorems for finite trigonometric sums, Adv. in Appl. Math. 29 (2002), 358-385', DOI 10.1016/S0196-8858(02)00020-9 — the same reference is carried in note `20216126` (Gittins et al. Part 1, Michigan Math. J. 74 (2024) 571-598). Note `240303445-evaluations-and-relations-for-finite-trigonometric-sums` is the current survey: Berndt, Kim & Zaharescu, arXiv:2403.03445, DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2403.03445. Note `spectral-invariants-for-polygons-and` (Ucar thesis full text) carries a section §3.4 titled 'Method of images and finite trigonometric sums' (thesis p. 103) which derives exactly these evaluations and itself cites [BY02] Berndt-Yeap.

findings.issue: Q4's Vandermonde-conditioning chain (§2.3) and its 'best match' (§2.4, Batenkov-Yomdin) omit the one paper in the vault whose hypothesis is literally the manuscript's regime: a PAIR of nearly-colliding nodes with the remaining nodes well separated. Batenkov-Yomdin Theorem 4.5 gives only 'roughly of the same order as some finite power of prod|xi_j - xi_i|^{-1}' — an unspecified power. The manuscript wants an explicit blow-up RATE as p->q with r well away, and the vault contains a paper that proves exactly that: linear growth in the inverse separation, with sharp constants independent of the number of nodes. Given the new §2.5 identification of det DF as the Vandermonde in the squared orders (p^2,q^2,r^2), the fit is exact rather than analogical, which makes the omission more conspicuous, not less. Separately, Moitra's bound is cited only second-hand through Aubel-Bolcskei, although the primary source is in the vault — a direct violation of the task's sourcing rule.
findings.evidence: Note `181208645-on-the-condition-number-of-vandermonde-matrices-with-pairs-of-nearly-c` — Kunis & Nagel, arXiv:1812.08645 (v2, Oct 2019), DOI 10.48550/arXiv.1812.08645, abstract verbatim: 'We prove upper and lower bounds for the spectral condition number of rectangular Vandermonde matrices with nodes on the complex unit circle. The nodes are "off the grid", pairs of nodes nearly collide, and the studied condition number grows linearly with the inverse separation distance. Such growth rates are known in greater generality if all nodes collide or for groups of colliding nodes. For pairs of nodes, we provide reasonable sharp constants that are independent of the number of nodes as long as non-colliding nodes are well-separated.' The note's own provenance line records why it was fetched: 'directly analogous to the manuscript's diagonal-approach blow-up'. Note `14081681-super-resolution-extremal-functions-and-the-condition-number-of-vanderm` is Moitra, arXiv:1408.1681, the primary source Q4 cites only via Aubel-Bolcskei.
findings.suggested_fix: In Q4-stability.md, anchor on the third bullet of §2.3, the one beginning '- Aubel & Bölcskei, arXiv:1701.02538', and add a fourth bullet immediately after it: '- **Kunis & Nagel, *On the condition number of Vandermonde matrices with pairs of nearly-colliding nodes*, arXiv:1812.08645** — the sharpest match to the manuscript's actual regime. Batenkov-Yomdin give the collision blow-up as "some finite power" of the gap product; Kunis-Nagel prove, for the case where exactly one PAIR of nodes nearly collides while the others stay well separated, that the condition number grows **linearly in the inverse separation**, with constants that are sharp and independent of the number of nodes. That is precisely the manuscript's diagonals ($p\to q$ with $r$ away), and it supplies the explicit rate that §6 needs rather than an unspecified exponent.' Then, in the same bullet list, change the Aubel-Bölcskei bullet's opening to cite Moitra primarily — 'Moitra, *Super-resolution, extremal functions and the condition number of Vandermonde matrices*, arXiv:1408.1681 (STOC 2015), recorded also by Aubel & Bölcskei, arXiv:1701.02538:' — so the large-sieve bound rests on the fetched primary source rather than a secondary report.

findings.issue: Q1's §5 closes with 'One caveat the manuscript should address': §5.3's birthday-paradox heuristic has 'no source in the fetched corpus' instantiating it, so 'either cite an instance or soften the claim'. That is under-informed — the corpus DOES hold the two ingredients such a heuristic needs, and a fetcher's own claims file says so explicitly. Q1 gives the author a bare instruction where it could give the two citations that discharge it. Since Q1 is the brief's highest-priority question and the heuristic is the only unsupported assertion left in §5, this is a real loss of coverage.
findings.evidence: `research/temp/claims-article-doivol62v62n1a17-revista-de-la-uma.json` states verbatim: 'The f_a(n) counting function defined in this paper -- the multiplicity of representations of a SINGLE fixed rational a/n as a sum of three unit fractions -- is structurally the building block a birthday-paradox heuristic for Section 5's coincidence-counting problem would need'. The source is note `article-doivol62v62n1a17-revista-de-la-uma`, Revista de la Unión Matemática Argentina, DOI 10.33044/revuma.1798, which 'gives an explicit closed-form formula for A_2(p) ... and a parametrization of length-3 Egyptian fractions yielding bounds for A_3(n), f_a(n), and F(n)'. Second ingredient: note `unit-fraction-partitions` (mathpages) tabulates the empirical multiplicities directly — `research/temp/claims-unit-fraction-partitions.json`: 'The number of unordered 3-part unit-fraction partitions of 1/k, U(k), for k=1..24 is given explicitly: U(1)=3, U(2)=10, ..., U(12)=160, ..., U(24)=366' and '9 primitive partitions of 5/12 and 5 of 7/12'. Neither note nor claim appears anywhere in the deliverables.
findings.suggested_fix: In Q1-diophantine-novelty.md, anchor on the paragraph opening '**One caveat the manuscript should address.**' and replace its closing sentence ('Either cite an instance or soften the claim.') with: 'Either soften the claim, or — better — build it from what does exist. The multiplicity function the heuristic needs is $f_a(n)$, the number of three-unit-fraction representations of a fixed rational $a/n$; explicit formulas and bounds for it are in the Revista de la Unión Matemática Argentina paper on ternary Egyptian fractions with prime denominator, DOI [`10.33044/revuma.1798`](https://doi.org/10.33044/revuma.1798), alongside Luca-Pappalardi\'s $x(\log x)^3 \ll \sum_{p\le x}A_3(p)\ll x(\log x)^5$. Empirical multiplicity data of exactly the required shape — the number of unordered three-part unit-fraction partitions of $1/k$ for $k\le24$ (3, 10, 21, 28, 36, 57, 42, 70, 79, 96, 62, 160, ...), and per-value counts such as 9 primitive partitions of $5/12$ against 5 of $7/12$ — is tabulated at mathpages, *Unit Fraction Partitions*. Framed that way the heuristic is a collision count over the $R$-value multiplicities, and §5.3 can cite a real counting function instead of an unattributed "standard in analogous Diophantine settings".'

findings.issue: Q2 never mentions Suleymanova, although the manuscript cites her (\bibitem{suleymanova2017}, arXiv:1701.01874) and the vault holds a four-note cluster on her work — including the fact, extracted during the sweep, that Schueth's 2026 paper (the manuscript's \bibitem{schueth2025}) identifies a specific COMPUTATIONAL ERROR in a published cone coefficient of hers. Q2's brief explicitly asks to 'record ... any sign or factor conventions that differ between them'; a documented wrong cone coefficient in a source the manuscript cites is squarely inside that remit and is absent. Q2 does flag the DGGW erratum for exactly this kind of reason; the Suleymanova correction is the same species of finding and is more directly about a cone coefficient.

findings.issue: Q3 §4's 'cautionary note' about erroneous isospectrality claims rests on a single instance, Maclachlan-Rosenberger 1994 as narrated second-hand by Linowitz-Voight. The vault holds a second, far closer instance that no deliverable uses: Gordon & Rossetti published a flat-3-pillow isospectrality assertion in Annales de l'Institut Fourier in 2003 and formally retracted it in a 2021 corrigendum in the same journal. That is (a) about a PILLOW — the manuscript's own object class, (b) in the orbifold-versus-manifold heat-invariant literature the manuscript sits inside, (c) an 18-year-delayed self-correction by two of Q5's designated referees, and (d) primary-sourced rather than narrated. It makes the cautionary argument stronger and better evidenced, and it is a citable pair the manuscript is currently missing.

findings.issue: Q1's OEIS section names only A334911 as the control. The vault's own OEIS claims file records that A334911 is the UNIQUENESS-restricted version and that the unrestricted analogue — 'at least two unordered triples of equal product and equal sum' — is A060292, with A337080 as a further cross-reference. A060292, not A334911, is the exact structural counterpart of the manuscript's own counting sequence (sums admitting at least one degeneracy), so it is the sequence a referee would look for and the template for an OEIS submission of the manuscript's numbers. The brief explicitly asks to 'Search OEIS for the counting sequences'; naming the right analogue sharpens the controlled null and gives §5 a concrete next step.

Source note: `a334911-oeis`. The deliverable's OEIS table and its 'control' row cite A334911 only; A060292 and A337080 appear nowhere in review/.

findings.issue: Q1 correctly rules out prior art and then recommends importing Schinzel's elliptic-curve technique from Guy D16 — the (e_1, e_3) problem — as 'the most promising route to improving' the manuscript's lower bound. But the vault holds a paper that applies the elliptic-curve method to the (sum, sum-of-reciprocals) pair itself, which is the manuscript's own pair of invariants rather than the dual one. It was fetched, triaged 'off-topic-tangential' and dropped. The triage is right about prior art and wrong about relevance to Q1's own recommendation: Q1 asks 'is any asymptotic count known or provable by standard methods?', and a worked elliptic-curve treatment of N = (sum)(sum of reciprocals) is the nearest existing instance of exactly the technique Q1 is recommending, applied to exactly these two symmetric functions.
findings.evidence: Note `160803382-integers-representable-as-the-product-of-the-sum-of-four-integers-with` — Yong Zhang, *Integers representable as the product of the sum of four integers with the sum of their reciprocals*, arXiv:1608.03382, DOI 10.48550/arXiv.1608.03382, abstract verbatim: 'By the theory of elliptic curves, we study the integers representable as the product of the sum of four integers with the sum of their reciprocals and give a sufficient condition for the integers with a positive representation.' The note's summary flags it 'TANGENTIAL, NOT ON POINT ... flagged only because it is the closest arXiv hit combining "sum" and "sum of reciprocals" of an integer tuple'. Note that any pair of triples sharing $S_1$ and $R$ automatically shares the product $S_1 R$, so Zhang's invariant is a consequence of the manuscript's matching condition, not an independent one.
findings.suggested_fix: In Q1-diophantine-novelty.md, anchor on the closing paragraph '**What §5 should add.**' and add a sentence before its final sentence: 'One further pointer, weaker but on the same technique: the elliptic-curve method has already been turned on the pair $(e_1, R)$ itself, not just on $(e_1,e_3)$ — Yong Zhang, *Integers representable as the product of the sum of four integers with the sum of their reciprocals*, arXiv:1608.03382, studies $N=(a+b+c+d)(\tfrac1a+\tfrac1b+\tfrac1c+\tfrac1d)$ by rational points on an associated curve. That is not prior art for §5 — it prescribes the *value* of a single 4-tuple\'s $S_1R$ rather than matching two triples — but any pair sharing $S_1$ and $R$ shares $S_1R$ automatically, so Zhang\'s setting is the degenerate one-tuple shadow of the manuscript\'s and is the closest existing worked example of the elliptic-curve route applied to these two symmetric functions specifically. Cite it alongside Schinzel when recommending that route.'

Bloom, *On a density conjecture about unit fractions*, arXiv:2112.03726 (v2, Oct 2023; appendix with Bhavik Mehta), status `evergreen`. Curated summary, verbatim: 'Proves: any set A of positive integers with positive upper density contains a FINITE subset S subset A with sum_{n in S} 1/n = 1, answering a question of Erdos and Graham. This is the "equal sums of unit fractions with no sum-of-denominators condition" branch of the literature (task's category (c)): it is about representing the single fixed value 1 ... rather than an exact counting or pairing question. Confirms no structural connection to Section 5's equal-sum-and-equal-reciprocal-sum pairing problem.' Q1 cites Bloom only as co-author of the Bloom-Elsholtz survey (arXiv:2210.04496, note `221004496-egyptian-fractions`), not this theorem.
